tasks.short: Watch the machine, its lights and gauges for malfunctions, write gauge readings on the hourly check sheet, and clear minor stops.

steps.what: Forming machine operator monitors machine operations and observes lights and gauges to detect malfunctions
Forming machine operator writes gauge readings on the hourly check sheet
Forming machine operator clears minor stops

tasks.design: Temperatures, pressures and cycle times are read from the machine control into the production system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) every hour and shown as control charts with alarms, so the operator does not write gauge readings on a check sheet. Watching the machine and clearing stops stay with the operator.
tasks.previous_blocker: Gauge readings were written on paper check sheets every hour.
tasks.enabler_now: SPC tools read gauges and PLCs and raise alarms.
tasks.still_hard: Older presses have no data link.
tasks.human_edge: Smelling burning material before any gauge moves.

evidence.claim: Q-DAS O-QIS reads gauges, CMMs and PLCs and gives control charts and alarms.
Per-operator production logs can monitor staff and need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the machine running to the stop cleared; repairs are outside.
Input contract: machine control linked; fallback is the check sheet.
Watching the machine does not change.
Readings are tied to the machine, not the operator.

incremental.description: Forming machine operator checks alarms for false triggers.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: older presses without data links; high: connected lines.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Check filaments against standards, decide the product fails, notify the supervisor, and record the reject.

steps.what: Forming machine operator checks extruded filaments against standards
Forming machine operator decides the filaments fail to meet standards
Forming machine operator notifies supervisors in person or by phone
Forming machine operator records the reject on the reject sheet

tasks.design: Rejects are captured on the machine terminal of the production system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) with a defect code, quantity and photo, which notifies the supervisor at once, so the operator does not fill a reject sheet and phone separately; serious defects are still discussed in person. Checking filaments and deciding they fail stay with the operator.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rejects were written on sheets and supervisors phoned or fetched.
tasks.enabler_now: MES defect capture records rejects and notifies supervisors.
tasks.still_hard: Borderline defects need the supervisor to look.
tasks.human_edge: Feeling that a filament is too brittle before it breaks.

reach.learn: Whether defects are reported at once.

evidence.claim: Critical Manufacturing MES captures defects and runs SPC.
Per-operator production logs can monitor staff and need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the product made to the reject recorded; root cause analysis is outside.
Input contract: defect codes set up; fallback is the reject sheet and phone.
Quality judgement stays with the operator.
Supervisors read notifications as they took calls.
research_questions: Do supervisors react sooner to defects?

incremental.description: Forming machine operator adds photos for unclear defects.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few rejects; high: unstable runs with many rejects.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read meters and counters, measure product dimensions, write quantities, types and dimensions on the production sheet, and type the sheets into the spreadsheet.

steps.what: Forming machine operator reads meters and counters
Forming machine operator measures dimensions of materials produced
Forming machine operator records production data on the production sheet
Forming machine operator types the production sheets into the spreadsheet at the end of the shift

tasks.design: Counters and meters are read from the machine control into the production system ({OPS_SYSTEM}), and digital gauges send measured dimensions straight to the run record, so the operator does not read meters, write a production sheet or type it into a spreadsheet at the end of the shift. Measuring products stays with the operator.
tasks.previous_blocker: Meters were read by eye, values written on sheets and typed in after the shift.
tasks.enabler_now: SPC tools read gauges and PLCs; MES record counts per run.
tasks.still_hard: Hand gauges without data output still need typing.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing a measurement that is right on paper but wrong in the hand.
tasks.altitude: The operator measures and checks instead of copying numbers.

evidence.claim: Q-DAS O-QIS reads gauges, CMMs and PLCs and links to SAP QM.
Per-operator production logs can monitor staff and need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the run in progress to data stored; planning is outside.
Input contract: machine control and gauges linked; fallback is paper sheets.
Works council consent comes before data are tied to operators.
research_questions: Do typing errors in production data disappear?

incremental.description: Forming machine operator types values from hand gauges without data output.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many hand gauges and older presses; high: connected lines with digital gauges.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read the work order and specification, look up the settings sheet, determine materials, settings and adjustments, and check the materials match the order.

steps.what: Forming machine operator reviews work orders and specifications on paper
Forming machine operator looks up the settings sheet for the product
Forming machine operator determines materials, settings and adjustments for the machine
Forming machine operator checks that the materials match the order

tasks.design: The work order, specification and recipe parameters for the product are shown on the machine terminal of the production system ({OPS_SYSTEM}), with parameters computed by fixed rules from the order, so the operator does not read paper orders and search settings sheets. Material lot labels are scanned and checked against the order. Determining settings and adjustments stays with the operator.
tasks.previous_blocker: Orders came on paper, settings sat on sheets and materials were checked by eye.
tasks.enabler_now: MES compute recipe parameters by rules and check scanned materials.
tasks.still_hard: New products have no settings history.
tasks.human_edge: Adjusting for a material batch that runs differently.

evidence.claim: Critical Manufacturing MES computes recipe parameters by business rules.

assumptions: Boundary: from the new order to materials checked; product design is outside.
Input contract: recipes loaded per product; fallback is settings sheets.
Setting decisions stay with the operator.

incremental.description: Forming machine operator reports recipe changes made at the machine.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: new products; high: repeat orders with set recipes.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The forming machine operator keeps watching machines, judging quality, measuring and setting up; check sheets, reject sheets, typed production data and paper orders shrink.
role.ambitious_version: An operator with more time on quality.
